summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing and shortlist open models for an initial HelixNova POC. Key success metrics: extraction F1 > 0.85 on domain testset, p95 latency <250ms for single-turn inference in hosted path or <100ms on Dedicated 4xA10s equivalent, cost target <$X per 1M tokens (TBD). Agreement to run a benchmark with HelixNova dataset and return results the week of 2026-11-23.
topics: Benchmarks and metrics (latency, throughput, hallucination rates)
Security & deployment mode (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Quick roll call, can you say who you have on the line?
00:08 Anya Kovalev: Hi, Anya here, Head of ML at HelixNova, Luis and Priya are on.
00:12 Luis Martinez: Hey all, Luis, platform eng.
00:15 Priya Singh: Priya, security.
:18 Ravi Patel: Ravi, I'll be the SE on the POC, focusing on benchmarking and model selection.
00:24 Maya Chen: Awesome. Agenda: align on success criteria, run through workloads, pick an open-model shortlist and tradeoffs, and agree timeline. Sound right?
00:31 Anya Kovalev: Yep that's it. We're mainly evaluating open models because of licensing and cost, and we need strong biomedical term handling and multi-lingual Spanish at a minimum.
00:41 Maya Chen: Great. To start, Anya, can you share your top success metrics?
00:45 Anya Kovalev: Sure. Primary is extraction accuracy — we want entity extraction and relation linking from clinical notes. Target F1 around 0.85 on our eval. Secondary is latency for interactive UI — ideally p95 under 250ms for hosted flows; if that's unrealistic we'll look at Dedicated. Also hallucination control — we need model to stay conservative, hallucination rate below 5% on curated prompts.
01:08 Maya Chen: Good. Ravi, from a serving perspective what do we recommend?
01:11 Ravi Patel: For extraction workloads we usually run a small prompt with a few-shot template, that means short context but sensitive tokens. For open models we can try a few families — Llama 2/3 variants, Mistral 7B/12B, Falcon 40B Instruct, and maybe Llama-derivative 70B quantized for quality. Tradeoffs: bigger models give better few-shot F1 but cost and latency rise. For p95 latency goals with hosted we typically need aggressive quantization + batching tuned, or choose Dedicated GPUs to hit <150ms.
01:41 Luis Martinez: Concurrency — we expect about 120 concurrent users at peak, average request size ~350 tokens with a 1.5s think time; rough estimate 30 reqs/sec sustained, bursts to 80. Does that change model choice?
01:56 Ravi Patel: Yes. For 30 rps sustained with 350-token responses, if you pick a 70B model even quantized, cost and throughput constraints push you to Dedicated. For hosted we recommend Mistral 12B or a Falcon 40B lightweight variant for balance. For Dedicated, Llama 70B quantized on 8xA10 or 4xH100 equivalent works.
02:19 Priya Singh: On security — we need SSO/SAML, SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and options for a VPC/private deployment. Any blockers on your side?
02:28 Maya Chen: We have SOC2 and audit logging, SAML SSO is supported; for private deployments we can run the control plane in HelixNova's VPC and provide on-prem options. We'll share the security pack after the call.
02:38 Anya Kovalev: Good. Let's step through the model shortlist. What do you recommend as a first pass?
02:43 Ravi Patel: Shortlist proposal: 1) Mistral Instruct 12B — good balance, strong multilingual support and cost-effective; 2) Falcon 40B Instruct — better on long-tail biomedical terms in our past evals but heavier; 3) Llama 2/3 70B quantized (ggml/or similar) — highest quality for few-shot extraction but needs Dedicated; 4) Mistral 7B fine-tuned small variant for low-latency flows. We also include a light distilled instruct model to check hallucination baseline.
03:12 Diego Rios: Any red flags in specialized biomedical language? Our corpus has lots of latinized terms and internal codes, will these open models handle that?
03:20 Ravi Patel: Models vary — in our internal benchmarks Mistral 12B and Falcon 40B generally handle specialized terms ok when you include a small in-context corpus; Llama 70B outperforms on zero-shot technical terminology but tradeoff is throughput. We'll run a domain adaptation pass and retrieval-augmented prompts to reduce hallucinations.
03:37 Maya Chen: On benchmarks, what metrics should we capture during the POC?
03:41 Ravi Patel: Recommended metrics: precision/recall/F1 on labeled extraction set, hallucination rate (manual sampling), p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, GPU memory footprint, and cost per 1M tokens. Also stability under concurrent load and cold-start latency. We'll output a benchmark spreadsheet.
04:00 Luis Martinez: For concurrency testing we can provide a 48-hour trace and a synthetic workload generator. We'll aim to reproduce a weekend run to test autoscaling.
04:08 Ravi Patel: Perfect — that'll help tune batching and cache settings. We'll test with and without KV cache and prefix caching for repeated contexts. Quick note: transcription sometimes shows K V cache spelled differently — but technically we'll test KV cache behavior.
04:22 Priya Singh: Data residency — patient data stays in EMEA and must not leave region. Can Redwood host in region?
04:29 Maya Chen: Yes, we have EMEA-region hosted clusters and Private install options. For sensitive PII we recommend Dedicated or Private and customer-managed keys into KMS/HSM. We'll add details to security docs.
04:40 Anya Kovalev: Timeline — we have an internal deadline to pick a model and decide on Dedicated by end of December. So what's realistic?
04:47 Maya Chen: If you can provide sample data and traces by 2026-11-13, we can run benchmarks week of 11-23, initial results by 11-27, and a decision meeting on 11-30. That fits your ask.
04:58 Ravi Patel: For the benchmark plan I'll propose three phases: phase 1 unit tests (accuracy and hallucination on heldout set), phase 2 performance under latency targets (single-turn and multi-turn), phase 3 stress tests for concurrency and autoscaling. We'll supply exact test harness and Docker images to run.
05:18 Diego Rios: Any constraints on inference input size? Our notes vary, some are long, up to 2,500 tokens.
05:23 Ravi Patel: That matters — Llama 70B and Falcon 40B handle longer context better; Mistral 12B might need retrieval chunking and shorter prompts. For long context use cases we can evaluate retrieval-augmented pipelines and local chunking to keep latency down.
05:40 Anya Kovalev: Cost targets — we've benchmarked internally and want cost under $Y per 1M tokens for inference to be viable. Can you ballpark?
05:47 Maya Chen: Ballpark depends a lot on model and deployment. Mistral 12B on hosted is usually X cheaper than Falcon 40B; Llama 70B on Dedicated can be economical at scale but requires commitment. We'll include explicit cost estimates in the pricing sheet.
05:59 Priya Singh: For auditing, will logs include per-request model version and prompt snapshots? We need that for traceability.
06:05 Maya Chen: Yes, we can include model version id, route, and request metadata; prompt snapshots are optional and we can redact according to policy. We'll map to your retention policy.
06:15 Anya Kovalev: Anything else on model tradeoffs?
06:17 Ravi Patel: One more thing — quantization strategy matters. 4-bit quant can drop quality slightly but improves latency. For extraction tasks sometimes the gap is small, so we'll run both FP16 and 4-bit quant runs. Also try LoRA fine-tuning on a small in-domain dataset to boost F1 without full retrain.
06:36 Luis Martinez: Sounds good. Priya, any security blockers?
06:39 Priya Singh: Not at this stage; need to review the SOC2 and SAML flow. Also want to confirm no logs leave region for the Private option.
06:47 Maya Chen: We'll send the security pack and a data residency checklist.
06:50 Anya Kovalev: Quick recap?
06:52 Maya Chen: Recap: Deliverables — 1) Model shortlist and recommended configs (Ravi) by 11-16; 2) security docs (Maya) by 11-15; 3) HelixNova provides sample data/traces by 11-13; 4) run benchmarks week of 11-23; 5) decision meeting 11-30. Success criteria reminder: F1 >= 0.85, p95 latency target <250ms hosted or <150ms Dedicated, hallucination rate <5%.
07:18 Anya Kovalev: Agreed, thanks.
07:20 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links to the benchmark spreadsheet and the deck.
07:25 Diego Rios: I'll look out for the benchmark plan.
07:28 Luis Martinez: Thanks all.
07:30 End of call.

Notes: Links referenced during call - Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood-internal.example/benchmarks/helixnova), Security pack (link: https://redwood-internal.example/security/helixnova-pack), Pricing sheet (link: https://redwood-internal.example/pricing/helixnova).
